1.why: All MFA endpoints use authorized() which binds the session cookie to session.userId and never accepts a client-supplied user identifier.

2.why: Identity OTPs are per-session, TOTP is verified against the authenticated user’s own encrypted secret, and backup codes are per-user hashes—codes do not work for other users.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets mfa.enabled and issues backups; no code invalidates other existing sessions for that user.

4.why: OTP secret is stored with AES-GCM encrypt(); backup codes are stored as salt+SHA-256 hash, not plaintext.

5.why: Secrets, session IDs, CSRF tokens, recovery codes, and OTPs are produced via crypto.getRandomValues / crypto.subtle.

6.why: Session is only in an HttpOnly cookie; client script never writes secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, recovery codes, and CSRF with strict regex/type checks before use.

8.why: Client esc() HTML-encodes all dynamic values before innerHTML; API responses are JSON, not raw HTML reflection.

9.why: Only redirect is a fixed 308 from HTTP to https://localhost:3000/; no user-controlled redirect targets.

10.why: secureHeaders/pageResponse set CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors DENY.

11.why: cookie() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Server errors are generic without stack traces, but the client deliberately console.logs and displays identity codes, test OTPs, and backup codes in a logs panel.

13.why: Identity codes expire in 5 minutes and set identityUsed; TOTP rejects reused counters; backup codes flip used=true after success.

14.why: Identity, TOTP, and recovery each lock for LOCK_MS after MAX_FAILURES (5) failed attempts.

15.why: New session IDs are issued on sign-in and after identity; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
